model_answer:
**Amazon (AMZN) — by a wide margin.**

Full-year 2025 capex plans/actuals:

| Company | 2025 capex |
|---|---|
| **Amazon (AMZN)** | **~$125B guided** (actual came in a bit higher, ~$128–132B depending on whether finance leases are included) |
| Alphabet (GOOGL) | $91–93B guidance, actual **$91.4B** |
| Meta (META) | $70–72B guidance, actual **$72.2B** (incl. finance-lease principal) |

Key details:
- **Amazon:** At Q3 2025 earnings (Oct. 30), CFO Brian Olsavsky said full-year 2025 cash capex would be **~$125B**, up from an earlier ~$118B outlook and $83B in 2024 — with the "vast majority" going to AWS/AI infrastructure (data centers, Trainium custom silicon, networking). He also flagged further growth in 2026, and on the Q4 call Jassy guided to **~$200B for 2026**.
- **Alphabet:** Started 2025 at $75B, raised to ~$85B in July, then to **$91–93B** in October; it reported **$91.4B** actual for 2025. It guided 2026 to **$175–185B**.
- **Meta:** Started at $60–65B, then $64–72B, then **$70–72B**; actual 2025 was **$72.22B**. It guided 2026 to **$115–135B**.

So Amazon was the biggest 2025 spender, roughly $35B+ above Alphabet and $55B+ above Meta — and it's also planning the largest 2026 budget (~$200B vs. Alphabet's $175–185B and Meta's $115–135B).

*(Note: definitions differ slightly — Meta and Amazon include finance-lease principal payments; Alphabet reports capex on a cash basis — but the ranking is unaffected.)*
